mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weeks (-20.1, -17.0, -16.6, -13.3), reflecting sustained recovery momentum in discretionary mobility that is expected to continue into the next four weeks absent any new shock.
evidence_refs: fact: three consecutive weekly increases in RETAIL_REC
failure_condition: The next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the last 28-day mean despite the prior three-week upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has declined steadily (8.1 to 5.1) indicating households are spending less time at home. If RESIDENTIAL drops below 5.0 for two consecutive weeks, this freed-up time will convert into increased discretionary retail visits within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 5.0 percent for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL declined from 8.1 to 5.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL falls below the 5.0 threshold but RETAIL_REC's next-period mean does not increase relative to the prior period.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-December pre-holiday shopping activity produces short-term spikes in RETAIL_REC independent of underlying restriction trends, consistent with the recent jump from -16.6 to -13.3; this seasonal lift should persist for at least one more week.
evidence_refs: fact: decision date 2020-12-15 falls within holiday shopping period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in the week immediately following the snapshot despite being within the holiday shopping period.

mechanism_narrative: A joint surge in PARKS (+11 points week-on-week) and modest TRANSIT improvement (+2.4 points) signals broader outdoor and commuting mobility normalization that should spill over into increased retail footfall within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT improves more than 2 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS rose from -21.9 to -10.9 and TRANSIT improved from -48.7 to -46.3 in the latest week
failure_condition: PARKS and TRANSIT both satisfy the trigger but the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean does not exceed the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained depressed and essentially flat (-21.3 to -19.1) across four weeks, indicating persistent remote-work policy or restrictions that suppress weekday commuting-linked retail traffic, keeping RETAIL_REC growth muted over the next month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -15 for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES values stayed between -21.3 and -19.1 over the last four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES stays below -15 throughout the period but the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean rises above the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has turned positive (0.7) while RETAIL_REC remains strongly negative (-13.3), suggesting consumers are substituting essential shopping trips for discretionary retail visits; continued divergence will keep discretionary retail recovery muted.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses above 0 while RETAIL_REC remains below -10
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM rose from -1.0 to 0.7 while RETAIL_REC stayed negative
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean rises substantially above the prior period, disproving the substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has improved for three consecutive weeks (-53.6 to -46.3); if this improvement accelerates to more than 3 points per week for two consecutive weeks, it signals loosening restrictions and return of commuting/errand trips, which should precede retail mobility gains within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves by more than 3 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT improved from -53.6 to -46.3 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT satisfies the acceleration trigger but RETAIL_REC's next 28-day mean does not increase relative to the prior period.

mechanism_narrative: Stagnant WORKPLACES mobility combined with falling RESIDENTIAL time suggests people are redirecting freed-up time away from home and work toward retail and recreation, producing a short-term uptick in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES changes by less than 1 point while RESIDENTIAL falls for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES held near -19 while RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.7 to 5.1
failure_condition: The trigger condition holds but RETAIL_REC's mean for the following week does not rise relative to the current week.
